PLC Language Quick Reference: Which One to Choose

A PLC language is a programming language used to write the control logic that a programmable logic controller executes in its scan cycle. IEC 61131-3 defines five of them: two graphical, two text based and one sequence oriented language that organises the others.

PLC languageFormLooks likeBest suited forStatus
Ladder Diagram (LD)GraphicalRelay contacts and coilsDiscrete on/off logic, interlocks, motor controlMost widely used
Function Block Diagram (FBD)GraphicalBlocks wired togetherPID loops, analog and continuous process controlWidely used
Structured Text (ST)TextHigh level code with IF, FOR, CASECalculations, data handling, complex algorithmsGrowing fast
Sequential Function Chart (SFC)Graphical sequenceSteps and transitionsBatch and step by step machine sequencesUsed for sequences
Instruction List (IL)TextAssembly style linesLegacy programs onlyDeprecated in the 2013 edition

Simple Way to Pick a PLC Language

  1. Mostly discrete signals and field electricians maintain it: use Ladder Diagram.
  2. Analog loops and process control: use Function Block Diagram.
  3. Heavy maths, arrays or recipe handling: use Structured Text.
  4. A machine or batch that moves through clear steps: use SFC, with actions in LD or ST.

Many projects mix languages, for example a Ladder main routine that calls Structured Text function blocks.
